discovery: Fluctuation theorems and the foundations of stochastic thermodynamics

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

motivation: The nominees discovered exact, universal laws that govern systems driven far from equilibrium, extending thermodynamics to small, fluctuating systems. Evans and co-workers found the fluctuation theorem (1993), which quantifies how often entropy-consuming trajectories occur. Jarzynski's equality (1997) relates the work done in irreversible processes to equilibrium free-energy differences. Seifert set up stochastic thermodynamics as a consistent framework, defining entropy production along single trajectories and establishing the integral fluctuation theorem. Later, with Barato, he derived thermodynamic uncertainty relations, which bound the precision of any current by its dissipation. These results are not approximations. They are exact identities and inequalities, confirmed in experiments on single molecules, colloids, electronic circuits and quantum dots. They now set the fundamental limits on precision, power and efficiency for molecular machines, nanoscale heat engines and quantum devices, and they underpin modern quantum thermodynamics.
